hero.name: Pranav
hero.who: a 40-year-old phone repair shop owner in Coimbatore who avoids every possible risk

story.b: For fourteen years, Pranav has run a small phone repair shop in Gandhipuram, Coimbatore. He repairs only one brand, because he knows it inside out. He buys every part from one wholesaler in Chennai. Nothing in the shop has moved in a decade. At home he drives his fifteen-year-old son Karthik to school, checks every homework page and sorts out every problem before Karthik even notices it. Then heavy rains shut the Chennai wholesaler for two weeks. Pranav has no parts and no backup. Customers drift to the new shop across the road. The same week, Karthik freezes and cries when a teacher scolds him, because he has never handled anything difficult alone.

ask.q: Pranav's carefully protected life has cracked at the first big shock. What question should he start asking?
o: How to protect himself even more tightly next time
How parts of his life could grow stronger from shocks instead of breaking
Whose fault the wholesaler's closure really was
ask.why: More protection made him depend on one supplier and one routine, which is exactly why one shock hurt so much. Blame changes nothing. Asking how his shop and family could gain from stress opens new choices, like more suppliers and more skills.

chapters.take: Avoiding every shock can leave you weaker when one finally comes.

story.b: One quiet afternoon, Pranav draws three columns in his accounts notebook. In the first he writes things that break under stress: one supplier, one brand, a son who has never been tested. In the second, things that survive stress unchanged: his savings, his loyal regular customers, the shop's good location. The third column is harder. What actually gets better when shaken? He thinks of his own hands. Every strange, difficult repair over the years has made him sharper. So he changes one habit at once. When a customer brings in a water-damaged phone of an unfamiliar brand, which he would have refused before, he says he will honestly try. It takes him two evenings, and he learns a lot.

ask.q: A customer brings Pranav an unfamiliar phone that other repairers have refused. Seen through this idea, what should he do?
o: Take it on honestly, since each tough repair can make his skills stronger
Refuse it, since a failed repair could hurt his reputation
Take it only if the customer pays double in advance
ask.why: Some things, like skill, improve from stress, so a hard repair is a chance to grow rather than a threat. Refusing keeps him comfortable but stuck, and demanding double money is about protection, not growth. Honest effort on hard jobs makes his skill grow stronger.

chapters.take: Some things break under stress, some survive, and some grow. Aim for the third.

story.b: Karthik asks if he can take the town bus to his tuition class in RS Puram. Pranav's first thought is no. Buses are crowded, routes are confusing, anything could happen. Then he remembers his third column. Small, safe challenges are how people get stronger. So he explains the route, writes the bus numbers on a card and makes sure Karthik's phone is charged. Then he lets him go. On the second day Karthik gets on the wrong bus, panics for a minute, asks the conductor and finds his way. He comes home buzzing with the story. On Saturday, Pranav lets him handle the shop counter for an hour, including one very grumpy customer.

ask.q: Karthik wants to take the town bus to tuition alone for the first time. What should Pranav do?
o: Keep driving him, since buses can be stressful
Follow the bus on his scooter, just to be safe
Let him go, after explaining the route and making sure he has a phone
ask.why: Small, safe challenges help children grow capable and confident, while removing every bump leaves them brittle. Driving him forever keeps him dependent, and secretly following sends the message he cannot cope. Basic preparation plus freedom gives him the right dose of stress.

chapters.take: Small, safe doses of stress make people stronger, not weaker.

story.b: Pranav's shop feels cramped and chaotic, and his evenings feel the same. His first idea is to add things: a billing app, a second assistant, a new display unit. Then he tries the opposite. He clears out the back shelf of old screens and covers that have not sold in years and gives the good ones to a repair class at a polytechnic. He stops answering the phone in the middle of delicate repairs and calls back later. At home, he stops scrolling through forwarded messages after nine. Nothing new is added. But the shop has room to breathe, repairs come out cleaner, and Pranav falls asleep earlier than he has in years.

ask.q: Pranav's evenings still feel crowded and tiring. Which choice best fits this idea?
o: Drop one draining habit, like late-night forwarded messages
Add a new evening routine of yoga, journaling and reading
Buy a fitness band to track how tired he is
ask.why: Adding routines or gadgets piles more onto an already crowded day. Often the bigger gain comes from subtraction. Removing one draining habit frees time and energy at once, with almost no cost and nothing new to manage.

chapters.take: Sometimes the best improvement is taking something away.

story.b: The night before his science exhibition, Karthik's model of a simple burglar alarm will not work. The bulb flickers and dies. Pranav, who repairs circuits every day, itches to grab the soldering iron and fix it in five minutes. He sits on his hands instead. He asks one question: where does the current stop? Karthik sighs, checks each joint with a borrowed tester and grumbles for half an hour. Then he finds a loose wire under the tape, fixes it and the bulb glows steadily. At the shop that week, Pranav does the same with his young assistant Senthil, who wires a charging port backwards. Pranav points to the problem and lets Senthil fix it himself.

ask.q: Karthik's science model keeps failing the night before submission. What should Pranav do?
o: Rebuild it himself, since he knows electronics best
Step back, ask a guiding question or two, and let Karthik find the fault
Tell Karthik to buy a ready-made model from the market
ask.why: Rebuilding or buying a model solves tonight's problem but takes away the learning that comes from finding the fault himself. Gentle questions keep Karthik in charge. Small failures he fixes alone teach far more than a perfect model someone else made.

chapters.take: Stepping back is often wiser than stepping in to fix everything.

story.b: Pranav now builds small options into his life, one at a time. He finds a second parts supplier in Madurai and places small orders there every month, so the relationship stays alive. He starts setting aside a little money every week, so one bad month cannot sink the shop. On Sunday evenings he learns laptop and tablet repair from videos and from an older technician friend in Peelamedu. Soon he is fixing three brands, not one. A few months later, the brand he once depended on launches phones with sealed parts that are hard to repair. The shop across the road struggles. Pranav barely notices, because his laptop repairs are already bringing in new customers.

ask.q: Pranav's friend runs a tailoring shop that depends on one school's uniform orders. What would protect him best?
o: Sign a longer contract with the school and relax
Lower his prices so the school never leaves
Build small options, like a few new customers, a new skill and some savings
ask.why: A longer contract or lower prices still leaves him tied to one customer, so one change could sink him. Small options cost little to build and give him choices when something shifts. If the school leaves, he has somewhere to go, and if a chance appears, he can take it.

chapters.take: Options give you a way out when things go wrong and a way in when chances appear.

story.b: The next monsoon, the Chennai wholesaler shuts again for ten days. This time Pranav simply calls Madurai, and the parts arrive by bus the next morning. The shop is busier than ever, partly with laptops now. The back shelf is still empty, and he likes it that way. Karthik takes the town bus everywhere and runs the counter every Saturday, handling grumpy customers better than his father does. When something at home goes wrong, Pranav waits a moment before rushing to fix it. Senthil now takes on the difficult repairs first. One evening Karthik asks his father to teach him soldering. Pranav hands him a broken phone and lets him make mistakes.

chapters.take: He stopped hiding from every shake, and his life grew stronger because of them.
